title: Docs: Add a glossary of open source terms to Git & GitHub 101
author: adiati98
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #1608 

<!--

That issue can be linked to the pull request by using the side panel in the Github UI or using the `#` symbol followed by the number of the associated issue.

To link a pull request to an issue to show that a fix is in progress and to automatically close the issue when someone merges the pull request, type the keyword "Closes" followed by a reference to the issue. For example, Closes #404 or Closes Virtual-Coffee/virtualcoffee.io/issues/404.

-->

## Description

This PR adds a "Glossary" section at the end of the Git & GitHub 101 guide. It explains 28 common open source terms in plain English, for example fork, clone, upstream, origin, fetch, pull, merge conflict, and pull request. It also covers terms that maintainers and contributors use, such as label, review, triage, and issue and pull request templates.

Changes in `src/content/resources/developer-resources/open-source/git-101.mdx`:

- A new "Glossary" section as the last section of the page.
- The terms are in alphabetical order, with a letter label above each group.
- One line at the end of the "Definitions" section links to the glossary.

title: Docs: Improve wording, steps, and images in Git & GitHub 101
author: adiati98
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #1604

<!--

If you have a pull request related to a current issue please link to that issue number.

That issue can be linked to the pull request by using the side panel in the Github UI or using the `#` symbol followed by the number of the associated issue.

To link a pull request to an issue to show that a fix is in progress and to automatically close the issue when someone merges the pull request, type the keyword "Closes" followed by a reference to the issue. For example, Closes #404 or Closes Virtual-Coffee/virtualcoffee.io/issues/404.

-->

## Description

This PR improves the "Git & GitHub 101" page so that it is clearer for first-time contributors and readers who are not native English speakers.

**Wording and style**

- Use plain English, active voice, and no contractions.
- Write procedures as numbered steps. Each step has an action sentence, then the code block, then the note about the placeholders.
- Use UPPERCASE placeholders, such as `REPO-URL`, `BRANCH-NAME`, and `DEFAULT-BRANCH`.
- Say once that the default branch is not always `main` or `master`.

**Corrections**

- Credentials: Git asks for them when you push. HTTPS needs a username and a Personal Access Token, because GitHub no longer accepts an account password for Git.
- Merge conflicts: they appear when you merge or open a pull request, not when you push.
- `git status` shows the state of your changes. It does not prove that a commit worked.
- The `upstream` remote is optional, because the page syncs the fork on GitHub.
- The async collaboration step now uses `git checkout -b BRANCH-NAME alice/BRANCH-NAME`.
- The co-author example explains that the terminal shows `>` and the reader does not type it.

**Merge conflicts**

- The section now has two separate procedures: simple conflicts on GitHub, and conflicts in the local repository.
- It says which conflicts GitHub can resolve in its web editor.
- It adds the steps that were missing: the **Accept** options, **Mark as resolved**, **Commit merge**, and saving the file.

**Images**

- Add screenshots for forking, cloning, syncing a fork, and resolving conflicts on GitHub and locally.
- Add descriptive alt text to every image.
- Host every image in the repository as a PNG. The profile screenshot and the first conflict image no longer load from an outside website.

**Headings**

The page URL does not change. Only the `#anchor` of these headings changes:

| Old anchor | New anchor |
| --- | --- |
| `#basic-workflows-to-contribute-to-the-open-source-using-git-and-github` | `#contributing-to-open-source-with-git-and-github` |
| `#create-a-new-branch` | `#creating-a-new-branch` |
| `#add-and-commit-changes` | `#adding-and-committing-changes` |
| `#fetching-upstream-changes` | `#syncing-your-fork-with-upstream` |
| `#resolve-merge-conflicts` | `#resolving-merge-conflicts` |
| `#push-changes` | `#pushing-changes` |
| `#asynchronous-collaboration-on-a-shared-branch-between-two-different-forks` | `#collaborating-asynchronously-on-a-shared-branch-between-two-different-forks` |
| `#synchronous-collaboration` | `#collaborating-synchronously` |
| `#how-does-it-work` | `#how-it-works` |

- "Check the Added Remote Repositories" is now part of "Adding an `upstream` Remote Repository".
- The small headings under "Add and Commit Changes" and under the async collaboration section are now numbered steps.
- Two new small headings: "Resolving Simple Conflicts on GitHub" and "Resolving Conflicts Locally".
- I searched the repository for links to the old anchors. Only in-page links used them, and this PR updates them.

This PR changes only `git-101.mdx` and its images.

title: Docs: Improve wording and fix outdated links in the Open Source guides
author: adiati98
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #1603

<!--

If you have a pull request related to a current issue please link to that issue number.

That issue can be linked to the pull request by using the side panel in the Github UI or using the `#` symbol followed by the number of the associated issue.

To link a pull request to an issue to show that a fix is in progress and to automatically close the issue when someone merges the pull request, type the keyword "Closes" followed by a reference to the issue. For example, Closes #404 or Closes Virtual-Coffee/virtualcoffee.io/issues/404.

-->

## Description

This PR improves the wording, links, and structure of three Open Source guides and the guides index page. The content of the guides stays the same. This PR does not add new topics.

Pages changed:

- About Open Source (`about-open-source.mdx`)
- Contributor Guide (`contributor-guide.mdx`)
- Maintainer Guide (`maintainer-guide.mdx`)
- Open Source index (`index.mdx`)

What changed:

- Fixed outdated links and terms. The discussion board link, the Hacktoberfest link, and the DigitalOcean tutorial link are updated. "Tags" is now "topics", and the old `CONTRIBUTIONS.md` references are removed.
- Used plain English: present tense, active voice, no contractions, fewer idioms, and shorter sentences.
- Fixed grammar, sentence fragments, and unclear sentences. The About and index lead text no longer starts with rhetorical questions.
- Formatted button and option names in bold (for example, **Issues** and **New issue**), and file names in code font. Removed color names used to identify buttons.
- Added an explanation for the "Relevant name" item in the Maintainer Guide checklist.
- Maintainer Guide: numbered the four sub-headings in "Documentation" and added a link to the pull request template. Updated the one link that points to them (the Contributor Guide link to "4. License").

Headings that changed:

| Page | Old heading | New heading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| About | Good to Know: Funding and Governance Models in Open Source | Funding and Governance Models in Open Source |
| Maintainer | Name, Description, Tags | Name, Description, Topics |
| Maintainer | The README, The Code of Conduct, The Contributing Guide, The License | 1. README, 2. Code of Conduct, 3. Contributing Guidelines, 4. License |
| Index | Guides Available: | Available Guides |

A heading change also changes its anchor (the `#section` part of the link). The pages keep the same URLs. I searched this repository and found no internal links to the old anchors, except one in the Contributor Guide, which this PR updates. Links from outside the repository to the old anchors would still open the page, but would not jump to the section. The anchors that other pages use (`#repository-checklist`, `#guide-to-writing-issues`, `#how-to-write-an-issue`) did not change.
